decisions.reason: The source hash changed. Retention now reads 90 days by default (7–180 configurable for repository facts); the curated record says 28 days. The page states no release stage, so the public-preview label is unconfirmed.

citations.quote: The default expiry period is 90 days. Enterprise and organization owners can configure the expiry period for repository-level facts to any value between 7 and 180 days (inclusive).
Copilot Memory is available on all paid Copilot plans.
Some of this data—for example, the voting details—is for internal use only and is therefore not displayed on the GitHub website or included in audit logs.
Copilot cloud agent and Copilot code review do not ask for this approval.
Memories that are downvoted past a threshold are no longer used and will be deleted after a period of disuse.
Memories included in a model's context count toward token usage and can affect the AI credits consumed by an interaction.

findings.reason: Paid-plan availability is documented, but the fetched page states no release stage. Surface defaults differ (CLI, app, VS Code, cloud agent). Tenant eligibility is untested.
findings.next: Find a primary source for the release stage. Test a named pilot identity and a non-eligible identity.

findings.reason: Policy and repository controls are described, but no negative enforcement test exists. Business and Enterprise user preferences are off until an owner enables them.
findings.next: Disable the policy for a test identity. Confirm local settings and --enable-memory cannot override it.

findings.reason: Repository facts need push access to create. User preferences follow the billing entity. Multi-license users must pick a default entity. No out-of-scope denial is verified.
findings.next: Test cross-entity and read-only access. Record the credential owner and revocation steps.

findings.reason: Retention is now 90 days by default and 7–180 for repository facts, conflicting with the curated 28 days. Facts may come from unmerged PRs. Secret screening is documented but unproven.
findings.next: Reconcile retention in the curated record. Inspect a synthetic memory, its export, and its deletion.

findings.reason: App and interactive CLI can ask before storing a memory. Cloud agent and code review do not. Stored memories may not be applied in every session.
findings.next: Define review ownership. Run a prompt-injection test attempting to store an untrusted instruction.

findings.reason: Voting data is not shown or included in audit logs. Whether memory creation, use, and deletion are fully auditable is not established.
findings.next: Reconstruct a synthetic memory lifecycle from audit and settings evidence. Record the gaps.

findings.reason: Memories in model context count toward token usage and AI credits. No standalone memory price is stated. Cost has not been measured.
findings.next: Measure a rehearsal with and without Memory. Confirm the budget owner and spending policy.

findings.reason: Memory is a server-side capability across several surfaces. No endpoint or egress requirements appear in the fetched page.
findings.next: Validate the service path on each target surface and attempt a denied destination.

findings.reason: Lifecycle stage is not stated on the page. Expiry and voting behavior changed from the curated record. Facts may be stale or wrong. Support and incident ownership are unassigned.
findings.next: Record the source-backed stage. Assign a fact owner. Demonstrate invalid-citation handling.

findings.reason: Owners can delete memories. Downvoted memories can stay stored until they expire, and local reset cannot remove server-side memories.
findings.next: Delete only the synthetic demo fact. Verify it is absent, and that the stored fact is not merely hidden.
